methodological_rigor.justification: This retrospective TMA-based study uses imaging mass cytometry (IMC) with single-cell spatial profiling of 530,728 cells across 82 NMIBC specimens (37 BCG responders, 45 nonresponders) and applies a graph attention multiple instance learning (IMC-GA-MIL) model. The IMC single-cell phenotyping with 18 cluster identification is technically sophisticated, and the plasma cell-dominant cluster association with progression (HR 2.28) is supported by appropriate Cox regression. However, the AI model is evaluated on only 10 patients (9/10 accuracy), making the 90% accuracy claim statistically unreliable. Both spatial and AI analyses are exploratory given the cohort size relative to model complexity.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: BCG response prediction in NMIBC is a high-priority unmet clinical need, and a spatial immune profiling approach that identifies plasma cell-dominant tumor microenvironment clusters as predictors of progression addresses a clinically meaningful question. The IMC-GA-MIL model's potential to predict BCG outcomes from tissue has practical appeal. However, the exploratory nature of the findings with very limited AI model validation (n=10) prevents any clinical translation claims; larger prospective validation is required.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is applicable for this biomarker-focused study. IMC panel composition, TMA construction, and cell phenotyping methodology are described with adequate technical detail. The IMC-GA-MIL model architecture is described with relevant hyperparameters. Some public datasets and code components may be accessible given the IMC methodology. However, the 10-patient test set for model evaluation without confidence intervals, and the absence of predefined cutpoints for cluster classification, represent gaps in REMARK compliance. Full data and trained model weights are not confirmed as publicly deposited.

novelty_literature.justification: Single-cell spatial immune profiling with IMC specifically applied to BCG response prediction in NMIBC with integration of a graph attention MIL model represents a substantial methodological novelty. While IMC has been applied in other cancer types, this specific application to NMIBC BCG outcomes with plasma cell spatial architecture as a predictor is a genuinely new contribution. The IMC-GA-MIL framework integrating spatial cell graph structure into outcome prediction is also methodologically innovative for urological oncology.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with clear sections addressing the clinical problem, IMC methodology, single-cell clustering, spatial analysis, and AI model development. The complexity of the IMC and MIL methodologies is communicated with appropriate technical detail without being inaccessible. UMAP visualizations and spatial distribution maps are informative. The discussion appropriately contextualizes the plasma cell finding within tumor immunology. The 10-patient model validation limitation could be more prominently acknowledged in the abstract.

key_strengths: Technically sophisticated single-cell IMC spatial profiling of 530,728 cells in 82 NMIBC specimens is a methodological advance for urological oncology biomarker research
Novel IMC-GA-MIL model integrating spatial cell graph structure for BCG outcome prediction represents a meaningful methodological contribution
Plasma cell-dominant cluster association with progression (HR 2.28) provides a biologically plausible and hypothesis-generating finding
High-dimensional single-cell phenotyping with 18 clusters provides a rich dataset for future reanalysis and hypothesis testing
key_concerns: AI model evaluated on only 10 patients (9/10 accuracy = 90%); this estimate has no statistical reliability and confidence intervals would span near-random to perfect accuracy
Retrospective TMA design without prospective validation limits the translational claims for BCG response prediction
REMARK requirements including predefined cluster cutpoints and confidence intervals for key performance metrics are not fully met
The 10-patient model test set size is presented without adequate uncertainty framing in the abstract and conclusions
chief_reviewer.rationale: This technically innovative spatial immune profiling study with a novel AI model makes a genuine methodological contribution to BCG response prediction research but is limited by the very small model validation set. Minor revisions should reframe the AI model findings as preliminary and provide confidence intervals or bootstrapped uncertainty estimates for the 10-patient test accuracy.
